# Gait loads: walk_treadmill

Data: Camargo, Ramanathan, Flanagan & Young (2021), J. Biomech. 119:110320, Mendeley Data v2 (10.17632/fcgm3chfff.2, k9kvm5tn3f.2, jj3r5f9pnf.2), CC BY 4.0. Processed here; the authors have not endorsed this work.

Run `gait.20261021-1445-walk_treadmill`, commit `fb60b388c1a6`, model `cfa2e0743e83`, spec `9da7d4a14e5a`, dataset manifest `ca427c3733c8`.

Assumptions:
- rigid at the standing pose from stand_static, arms at the sides; arm swing is not modelled
- root rule pelvis_dataset: the dataset's pelvis translation scaled by leg-length ratio
- pelvis pitch mean: measured (anterior-positive offset 0.0 deg); trunk mode(s): rigid, counter_rotate
- pelvis frame offset: measured (the dataset's IK pelvis frame against the model's Dumas pelvis frame; decisions/0004)
- treadmill: the model walks in place, the belt carries the ground backward; no friction-cone or slip enforcement on the kinematics
- methods A and H take the CoP relative to the subject's pelvis, scaled by leg-length ratio
- joint limits and contacts are disabled in inverse dynamics; frames past a limit are not clipped
- toe: the dataset's foot is rigid, so method A holds the toe welded flat (the ankle carries the whole-foot moment); in B and H the toe rolls with its foot (rolling rule: while the foot is in stance, as the dataset flags it, and pitched heel-up, the toe takes the angle of the foot's sole to the floor, otherwise 0; low-passed with the other signals). The toe's stiffness and damping do not enter its motion, only the toe joint's own torque row; the ground force acts on the toe where the CoP is ahead of the hinge. Not a model of a measured toe angle.

Cells are mean / 95th percentile / maximum across subject-strides, offset subjects AB13, AB15 included unless a table says otherwise. B = Freyja's own dynamics, A = measured force and CoP scaled (native / filtered like the kinematics), H = own total force at the measured CoP. Trunk mode columns: rig = rigid, cr = counter_rotate (`rigid` is a locked spine; `counter_rotate` is an actuated lumbosacral roll and yaw cancelling the pelvis's roll and yaw by feed-forward; `first_harmonic` is a human-like reference point from the trunk IMU, a diagnostic and never a record mode; no mode is the v1 headline, so every row that depends on the trunk names its mode). A's leg rows do not depend on the trunk mode (tested), so A shows one column. Joints above the pelvis are the same for every method and are listed by mode. The band pools both limbs: correlation >= 0.9 and RMS <= 15% of the dataset's peak-to-peak for the sagittal hip, knee and ankle. No other pass or fail.
